grammar.label: the present tense for claims in academic citation
grammar.meaning: a published claim is treated as still standing

explanation.en: 'Karimova argues that the date is wrong' uses the present even though she wrote it years ago, because the argument is still on the table. The past tense is kept for what happened in the study: 'She interviewed forty teachers.'
explanation.uz: 'Karimova argues that…' — hozirgi zamon, chunki fikr hozir ham kuchda. O'tgan zamon esa tadqiqotda nima qilinganini bildiradi.

grammar.positive_example: Karimova argues that the earlier date is wrong; she examined sixty manuscripts.
grammar.negative_example: Karimova argued that the earlier date was wrong, so her claim no longer stands.

l1_notes.uz: Zamon tanlovi ma'no tashiydi: hozirgi zamon — fikr hali kuchda, o'tgan zamon — bajarilgan ish.

grammar.label: reporting verbs carry a stance
grammar.form: claims / demonstrates / concedes / alleges / notes + that-clause
grammar.meaning: the verb tells the reader what the writer thinks of the claim

explanation.en: 'Shows' accepts the claim, 'claims' holds it at arm's length, 'concedes' says it was given up reluctantly, 'notes' is neutral. Choosing one is taking a position, so it must be done on purpose.
explanation.uz: 'shows' — qabul qiladi, 'claims' — masofa saqlaydi, 'concedes' — istamay tan olishni bildiradi, 'notes' — betaraf. Fe'l tanlash — pozitsiya bildirish.

grammar.positive_example: The author claims, but does not show, that the figures are reliable.
grammar.negative_example: The author shows, but does not prove, that the figures are reliable.

l1_notes.uz: Neytral ko'ringan fe'llar ham baho tashiydi; ularni tasodifan tanlash matnni noto'g'ri ranglaydi.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Your sentence says 'Karimova argued in 1998 that the roads were built too late'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And the argument is still on the page. 'Karimova argues that the roads were built too late.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Present tense for a paper written before I was born?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The paper is still speaking. That is the whole reason we cite it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then in the next line I have 'Karimova says'.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Says' tells the reader nothing. Does she show it, claim it, or concede it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: She shows it. She has the figures for four districts.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then write 'shows'. And the man who disagrees with her?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: He has no figures at all. He alleges that the records were changed.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Alleges' is exactly right. You have judged him in one word, and you have not said he is wrong.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is fair if it is true. A reporting verb carries your stance whether you choose it or not, so choose it.
